analysis.title: Global Credit: What We're Watching
key_insights: US IG index spreads widened 2bp last week for an excess return of -0.1% but have outperformed leveraged credit and European credit. MS expects the resilience to persist even if rates rise further, backed by higher all-in yields and insurance demand.

AI capex funding should stay concentrated among high-quality hyperscalers, which account for more than 75% of 2027/28 AI capex and are less sensitive to higher rates. Spreads on lower-rated names, data center construction bonds and neoclouds should stay volatile through 2027.

MS expects the US IG curve to flatten near term as the next wave of AI capex shifts toward chips, which adds short-dated financing needs and front-end supply. Front-end issuance (under 5 years) is about 50% of the trailing three-month total.

Trade: go long the CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche versus the index, delta-hedged 1:8x, to position for compression in AI-related credit risk. AI basket CDS spreads are about 40bp wider over the past month and trade more than 85bp wider than CDX IG.
The key risk to the equity tranche trade is a further deterioration in sentiment on AI names, which would push spreads wider and make the tranche underperform the index.

US HY stress is concentrated in telecom and media. Cable & Satellite TV and Wireline Telecom make up $33bn, about 35% of the $95bn trading above 1000bp. Altice/CSC Holdings is the largest issuer at $15.5bn and 5,200bp.

Only 76 US HY issuers trade above 1000bp. The top 5 make up 32% of distressed face value and the top 10 make up 43%. 2028-2030 maturities are 72% of the distressed group, and 2028 maturities total $10.9bn at about 6,300bp.

About $34bn (35%) of today's distressed bonds were below 1000bp three months ago, across 30 issuers including XRX, IHRT, VMED, Ziggo, JBLU, SABHLD, MPW and WHR. Another roughly $146bn (10% of the index) trades at 500-1000bp, led by telecom ($29bn) and media ($25bn).

US HY spreads widened 3bp last week with a positive excess return of 0.1%, and Single Bs underperformed. Loans tightened 6bp for a +0.4% total return. HY had inflows of $1.29bn while IG (-$0.30bn) and loans (-$0.30bn) had outflows.
US IG primary priced $60bn last week, helped by the first hyperscaler deal since August. YTD supply is $1,987bn in IG (+27% y/y), $275bn in HY (-2% y/y) and $355bn in loans (-11% y/y).
EUR IG spreads tightened 4bp last week for an excess return of +0.22%. EUR HY spreads tightened 12bp for +0.56%, with European HY funds taking in $460m, the strongest weekly figure since July.
Asia credit spreads widened 5bp last week. Asia HY widened 31bp and Asia IG 1bp. China HY widened 118bp over the week.

US equities and credit sold off last week, led by technology on concerns about returns on AI capex. Treasuries rallied on safe-haven demand. The Fed and ECB held rates, and UK gilts rallied after the Budget.

Within US IG, Broadcom (AVGO) bonds are the worst single-A performers, 51-59bp wider month to date. Oracle (ORCL), Charter (CHTR) and SPCX bonds are among the worst BBB performers, 60-95bp wider month to date.
Oil is at $100.7 WTI and $110.1 Brent, up 81% and 93% YTD. The US 10-year yield is 4.93% and the 30-year is 5.31%.

market_movers.rationale: Broadcom single-A bonds fill the worst-performer lists, with spreads 51-59bp wider month to date and 125-166bp in level. The report gives no rating call.

sector_views.rationale: IG is expected to move from supply-driven underperformance to a relative safe haven on high all-in yields and insurance demand.
These sectors are the epicenter of HY stress, with Cable & Satellite TV and Wireline Telecom at about 35% of the $95bn trading above 1000bp.

earnings_insights: The report says AI capex returns concerns, heightened by earnings, drove last week's tech-led US equity and credit selloff. It gives no company-level figures.

trade_ideas.description: Long CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche versus CDX IG index, delta-hedged 1:8x
trade_ideas.rationale: Express a view on compression in AI-related credit risk through the broader market rather than specific AI names, since the sell-off has gone too far.
trade_ideas.risk: Further deterioration in sentiment around AI names drives another leg wider in spreads and the equity tranche underperforms the index.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in AI sentiment widening spreads again.
Higher rates and heavy IG supply.
Volatile spreads on lower-rated AI borrowers, data center construction bonds and neoclouds through 2027.
Distress concentrated in telecom and media, with 2028-2030 maturities making up 72% of the distressed group.
vol_and_positioning: CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche is at 921bp and CDX IG is at 62bp. AI basket CDS is more than 85bp wider than CDX IG.
The share of the CCC index trading at distressed levels is at the 70th percentile versus history.
Non-dealer CDS positioning as of Oct 23: net positioning in all CDX IG series is 136.4bn and in all CDX HY series 26.4bn.
US CCC spreads are 1,116bp, at the 99th percentile of the 1-year range and 5-year wides. US HY spreads are 340bp, at the 100th percentile of the 1-year range.
geopolitical: US midterm elections this week, with implications expected to be more micro than macro.
UK Budget, followed by a gilt rally.

tension_points.bull_case: MS argues the AI-related credit sell-off has gone too far. Long CDX IG 0-3% versus the index is meant to capture compression in AI credit risk, and high-quality hyperscalers are insulated from rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment on AI names could worsen, driving another leg wider in spreads. Lower-rated AI borrowers, data center construction bonds and neoclouds stay volatile through 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further deterioration in sentiment around AI names that drives another leg wider in spreads and makes the equity tranche underperform the index.
